Age-sex pyramid of confirmed dengue cases

Source: R/plt_pyramid.R
plt_pyramid.Rd

Builds a population pyramid of confirmed dengue cases from the SINAVE dataset, with males on the left, females on the right and the age groups in the centre. Each side is headed by a Font Awesome icon and the total number of cases by sex, which act as the legend.

plt_pyramid(
  data,
  col_male = "#0072B2",
  col_female = "#CC79A7",
  gap = 0.18,
  size_age = 3.5,
  size_count = 3,
  icon_male = "person",
  icon_female = "person-dress",
  show_zero = FALSE,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = "Fuente: SINAVE/DGE, Secretaría de Salud."
)

Arguments

data

data.frame with the SINAVE dengue dataset. It must contain the columns `ESTATUS_CASO`, `IDE_SEX`, `IDE_EDA_ANO`, `CVE_EDO_REP` and `CVE_MPO_REP` (names are standardised with [janitor::clean_names()]). Only confirmed cases (`ESTATUS_CASO == 2`) are used.

col_male

colour for males (default `"#0072B2"`, Okabe-Ito blue).

col_female

colour for females (default `"#CC79A7"`, Okabe-Ito reddish purple).

gap

width of the central space for the age labels, as a proportion of the largest count (default 0.18). Increase it if the labels look crowded.

size_age

text size of the age-group labels (default 3.5).

size_count

text size of the number of cases (default 3).

icon_male, icon_female

names of free Font Awesome icons drawn above each side (default `"person"` and `"person-dress"`; other options are `"mars"`/`"venus"` or `"child"`/`"child-dress"`). See <https://fontawesome.com/search?ic=free>.

show_zero

logical. If TRUE, age groups without cases are labelled with 0 (default FALSE).

title, subtitle

plot title and subtitle (default NULL, none).

caption

plot caption (default cites SINAVE/DGE).

Value

a ggplot object.

Details

Ages are grouped into 15 classes: `<1`, `1-4`, `5-9`, ..., `60-64` and `65+` (intervals are closed on the left). Age groups without cases are kept with a count of 0, so the pyramid never has gaps. The number of cases is printed inside each bar when it fits and outside otherwise. The x axis shows absolute counts on both sides.

Icons are rendered from SVG with fontawesome and rsvg, so no system font is required and they are kept when saving with [ggplot2::ggsave()].

See also

[fontawesome::fa()]

Author

Felipe Antonio Dzul Manzanilla felipe.dzul.m@gmail.com

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- data.table::fread("DENGUE2_.txt", quote = "", fill = TRUE)

plt_pyramid(data = x,
            title = "Casos confirmados de dengue por grupo de edad y sexo",
            subtitle = "Jalisco, 2026")

# other colours and icons
plt_pyramid(data = x,
            col_male = "#1B9E77", col_female = "#D95F02",
            icon_male = "mars", icon_female = "venus",
            show_zero = TRUE)

ggplot2::ggsave("pyramid.png", width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
} # }
